His prophecy proved tragically accurate. The exorbitant reparations caused hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic, obliterating the middle class and fostering a profound sense of national humiliation. This environment of economic despair and revanchism provided highly fertile ground for the rise of totalitarianism, ultimately paving the path to a far more devastating global conflict.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The diplomatic brilliance of the Allied powers in neutralizing the German military threat.
John Maynard Keynes's success in preventing the economic collapse of the Weimar Republic.
The catastrophic economic and political consequences of the punitive post-war reparations.
The reasons why the Treaty of Versailles was universally praised in the early 20th century.
answer: The catastrophic economic and political consequences of the punitive post-war reparations.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय वर्साय की संधि (Treaty of Versailles) के दंडात्मक (punitive) प्रभावों का वर्णन करना है। यह बताता है कि कैसे भारी जुर्माने और प्रतिशोध ने जर्मनी को आर्थिक रूप से नष्ट कर दिया और अंततः द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध (totalitarianism) का मार्ग प्रशस्त किया। विकल्प C इस विषय का सही सारांश है।
trick: Main Theme हमेशा कारण और प्रभाव (Cause and Effect) को जोड़ता है। कारण: 'punitive terms' (दंडात्मक शर्तें), प्रभाव: 'economic despair' और 'rise of totalitarianism' (विनाशकारी परिणाम)।
tip: ऐतिहासिक संधियों की आलोचना वाले अनुच्छेदों में, विषय अक्सर यह होता है कि कैसे 'अत्यधिक कठोर नीतियां' (Harsh policies) भविष्य की आपदाओं (Future disasters) का कारण बनती हैं।

passage: The 'bystander effect' is a well-documented social psychological phenomenon where individuals are less likely to offer help to a victim when other people are present. Originally studied following the infamous murder of Kitty Genovese in 1964, researchers found that the probability of intervention is inversely related to the number of bystanders. This counterintuitive behavior is primarily driven by the 'diffusion of responsibility.' When an individual is alone, the moral burden to act rests entirely on their shoulders. However, in a crowd, this responsibility is psychologically distributed among all onlookers. Everyone assumes that someone else—perhaps someone more qualified—will intervene, resulting in a collective paralysis where no one acts at all.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred about the 'diffusion of responsibility'?
options: It makes individuals more courageous when they are surrounded by a large crowd.
It decreases an individual's sense of personal accountability in group settings.
It proves that human beings are naturally malicious and enjoy watching others suffer.
It only occurs when bystanders lack the physical strength to help a victim.
answer: It decreases an individual's sense of personal accountability in group settings.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि भीड़ में जिम्मेदारी सभी लोगों के बीच बँट (distributed) जाती है, जिससे हर कोई सोचता है कि कोई और मदद करेगा। इससे यह अनुमान लगाया जा सकता है कि 'डिफ्यूजन ऑफ रिस्पॉन्सिबिलिटी' (जिम्मेदारी का फैलाव) समूह सेटिंग्स में व्यक्ति की व्यक्तिगत जवाबदेही (personal accountability) की भावना को कम कर देता है।
trick: 'moral burden... is psychologically distributed among all onlookers' का सीधा अर्थ है 'decreased personal accountability' (व्यक्तिगत जवाबदेही में कमी)।
tip: मनोविज्ञान (Psychology) के प्रश्नों में Inference हमेशा मानव व्यवहार के उस तंत्र (mechanism) का वर्णन करता है जिसे गद्यांश समझा रहा है (यहाँ: भीड़ में लोग जिम्मेदारी से बचते हैं)।

passage: For over a century, the central dogma of neuroscience held that the adult mammalian brain was structurally complete and incapable of generating new neurons—a state known as 'post-mitotic.' It was believed that humans were born with a finite number of brain cells that slowly died off with age. However, revolutionary research in the late 20th century definitively overturned this paradigm, proving the existence of 'adult neurogenesis.' Scientists discovered that neural stem cells in specific brain regions, particularly the hippocampus (which governs learning and memory), continue to produce functional neurons throughout an individual's entire lifespan. This groundbreaking discovery has profoundly shifted the focus of neurological research toward understanding how exercise, diet, and environmental enrichment can stimulate the birth of new brain cells, offering new hope for treating neurodegenerative diseases.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The biological reasons why the human brain loses cells as a person ages.
The superiority of late 20th-century microscopes in discovering neural stem cells.
The overturning of the neurological dogma that adult brains cannot generate new neurons.
The methods by which neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's can be completely cured.
answer: The overturning of the neurological dogma that adult brains cannot generate new neurons.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय इस पुरानी वैज्ञानिक मान्यता (dogma) का खंडन (overturning) है कि वयस्क मस्तिष्क नए न्यूरॉन्स नहीं बना सकता। गद्यांश बताता है कि कैसे 'एडल्ट न्यूरोजेनेसिस' की खोज ने न्यूरोलॉजी के इस पुराने प्रतिमान (paradigm) को पूरी तरह से बदल दिया।
trick: गद्यांश का पहला आधा भाग पुरानी मान्यता बताता है और 'However' के बाद नई खोज ('overturned this paradigm') का वर्णन करता है। थीम हमेशा इस 'बदलाव' (Shift/Overturning) पर केंद्रित होगी।
tip: वैज्ञानिक खोजों वाले अनुच्छेदों में, थीम अक्सर 'Paradigm shift' (पुराने सिद्धांत का गलत साबित होना और नए का आना) होती है।

passage: Italian Marxist philosopher Antonio Gramsci developed the theory of 'cultural hegemony' to explain why the working class had not inevitably overthrown capitalism, as Karl Marx had predicted. Gramsci argued that the ruling capitalist class maintains its power not primarily through coercive state force (the police or military), but rather through the ideological control of cultural institutions—such as schools, the church, and the media. By heavily influencing these institutions, the bourgeoisie disseminates its own values, beliefs, and worldview until they become accepted as the 'common sense' of the entire society. Consequently, the oppressed working class unwittingly internalizes the very ideology that subjugates them, viewing the unequal social order as natural and unchangeable rather than an artificial construct designed to exploit them.
question: It can be inferred from the passage that, according to the theory of cultural hegemony, the ruling class:
options: Relies entirely on military violence to prevent the working class from rebelling.
Manipulates societal values to make their dominance seem natural and consensual.
Actively encourages the working class to develop their own independent cultural institutions.
Failed to prevent the working class from overthrowing capitalism in the 20th century.
answer: Manipulates societal values to make their dominance seem natural and consensual.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि शासक वर्ग (ruling class) सांस्कृतिक संस्थानों के माध्यम से अपनी विचारधारा को फैलाता है ताकि वे पूरे समाज के लिए 'सामान्य ज्ञान' (common sense) बन जाएं, और शोषित वर्ग इस असमान व्यवस्था को 'प्राकृतिक' (natural) मान ले। इससे अनुमान निकलता है कि शासक वर्ग अपने प्रभुत्व को स्वाभाविक और सर्वसम्मति वाला (natural and consensual) दिखाने के लिए सामाजिक मूल्यों में हेरफेर (manipulate) करता है।
trick: वाक्यांश 'accepted as the common sense' और 'viewing the unequal social order as natural' सीधे तौर पर विकल्प B के 'natural and consensual' से मेल खाते हैं।
tip: समाजशास्त्र (Sociology) के गद्यांशों में 'Hegemony' या 'Ideology' का मतलब हमेशा 'विचारों के माध्यम से नियंत्रण' (control through ideas) होता है, हथियारों के माध्यम से नहीं।

passage: The traditional industrial economy operates on a linear 'take-make-dispose' model, which relentlessly extracts raw materials, converts them into short-lived consumer goods, and ultimately dumps them into overflowing landfills. In stark contrast, the emerging concept of the 'circular economy' envisions a closed-loop system inspired by natural biological cycles. In a true circular economy, the concept of 'waste' is entirely eliminated. Products are intentionally designed for durability, reparability, and complete material recovery. Biological materials safely re-enter the biosphere to rebuild natural capital, while technical materials—such as metals and plastics—are endlessly recycled into new products without degrading in quality. Proponents argue this systemic shift is not merely an environmental imperative, but a massive economic opportunity that decouples economic growth from the finite consumption of natural resources.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The inevitable collapse of the global economy due to the exhaustion of raw materials.
The technological methods used to recycle low-quality plastics into consumer goods.
The transition from a linear, wasteful industrial model to a regenerative, circular economic system.
The reasons why the 'take-make-dispose' model is economically superior to natural biological cycles.
answer: The transition from a linear, wasteful industrial model to a regenerative, circular economic system.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय पारंपरिक 'रैखिक' (linear / take-make-dispose) अर्थव्यवस्था की आलोचना करना और इसके विकल्प के रूप में 'सर्कुलर इकॉनमी' (circular economy) का वर्णन करना है, जहाँ कचरे को खत्म कर दिया जाता है और सामग्रियों का पुन: उपयोग (regenerative system) किया जाता है। विकल्प C इस पूरे तुलनात्मक विषय का सटीक सारांश है।
trick: Main Theme गद्यांश की संरचना का पालन करता है: 'Linear model' -> 'In stark contrast' -> 'Circular economy'. थीम में दोनों का उल्लेख होना चाहिए।
tip: पर्यावरण अर्थशास्त्र (Environmental economics) में, थीम हमेशा 'Sustainable/Regenerative' (टिकाऊ) मॉडल के लाभों को दर्शाती है।

passage: For decades, evolutionary biology was dominated by the idea that complex life evolved almost exclusively through gradual, competitive genetic mutations. However, Lynn Margulis revolutionized this view with her 'Endosymbiotic Theory.' Margulis proposed that eukaryotic cells (the complex cells that make up plants, animals, and humans) did not evolve merely by mutating, but by cooperating. She argued that key cellular organelles, specifically mitochondria and chloroplasts, were once free-living bacteria that were engulfed by larger host cells. Instead of digesting the prey, the host formed a mutually beneficial symbiotic relationship with it. The engulfed bacteria provided energy, while the host provided protection. Over millions of years, these organisms merged into a single, indivisible entity. Initially ridiculed, this theory is now widely accepted, fundamentally shifting evolution from a story solely of brutal competition to one heavily reliant on merging and cooperation.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred from the Endosymbiotic Theory?
options: Evolution is driven entirely by aggressive competition and the destruction of weaker organisms.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts still possess the ability to survive outside of a host cell today.
Complex eukaryotic life evolved through a process of biological cooperation and integration.
Bacterial cells are structurally identical to the cells that make up human beings.
answer: Complex eukaryotic life evolved through a process of biological cooperation and integration.
explanation: गद्यांश स्पष्ट रूप से बताता है कि लिन मार्गुलिस के सिद्धांत ने विकासवाद को केवल 'क्रूर प्रतिस्पर्धा' (brutal competition) की कहानी से हटाकर 'विलय और सहयोग' (merging and cooperation) पर आधारित कर दिया। इसका सीधा अनुमान यह है कि जटिल यूकेरियोटिक जीवन (eukaryotic life) जैविक सहयोग और एकीकरण (integration) की प्रक्रिया के माध्यम से विकसित हुआ।
trick: अंतिम वाक्य ('shifting evolution from a story solely of brutal competition to one heavily reliant on merging and cooperation') सीधे विकल्प C की ओर इशारा करता है।
tip: वैज्ञानिक गद्यांशों में यदि कोई नया सिद्धांत पुरानी मान्यता ('competition') को गलत साबित करता है, तो Inference हमेशा नए सिद्धांत की मुख्य खोज ('cooperation') पर आधारित होगा।

passage: Transhumanism is a philosophical and intellectual movement that advocates for the use of advanced technologies to greatly enhance human intellect and physiology, ultimately aiming to conquer aging and death. By utilizing genetic engineering, cybernetics, and brain-computer interfaces, transhumanists envision a future where humanity forcefully seizes control of its own evolution, transitioning into a 'post-human' species. While proponents view this as the ultimate liberation from our fragile biological constraints, the movement raises profound bioethical concerns. Critics warn of an impending 'genetic divide,' wherein only the ultra-wealthy will be able to afford cognitive and physical upgrades, creating a permanently bifurcated society. Furthermore, philosophers question whether shedding our biological vulnerabilities might simultaneously strip away the empathy and shared mortality that fundamentally define the human experience.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The biological mechanisms by which genetic engineering can completely halt the aging process.
The philosophical and ethical implications of using technology to artificially accelerate human evolution.
The economic cost of developing brain-computer interfaces for the global population.
The definitive proof that transhumanism will destroy all human empathy and morality.
answer: The philosophical and ethical implications of using technology to artificially accelerate human evolution.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय ट्रांसह्यूमनिज़्म (Transhumanism) है, जो तकनीक का उपयोग करके मानव विकास (evolution) को तेज़ करने की वकालत करता है। गद्यांश इसके लाभों (उल्लेखनीय मुक्ति) और इससे जुड़ी गंभीर नैतिक व दार्शनिक चिंताओं (असमानता, मानवता का खोना) दोनों पर चर्चा करता है। विकल्प B इस समग्र विषय को समेटता है।
trick: विकल्प D 'definitive proof' (निश्चित प्रमाण) जैसे चरम शब्दों का उपयोग करता है, इसलिए यह गलत है। विकल्प B संतुलित है और 'philosophical and ethical implications' (दार्शनिक और नैतिक प्रभाव) को कवर करता है, जो पूरे गद्यांश का सार है।
tip: नई तकनीकों (Emerging technologies) पर आधारित अनुच्छेदों में थीम हमेशा तकनीक के 'Ethics/Implications' (नैतिक प्रभाव और परिणामों) के इर्द-गिर्द घूमती है।

passage: In international relations, the concept of 'soft power,' coined by political scientist Joseph Nye, stands in stark contrast to the 'hard power' of military coercion and economic sanctions. Soft power is the ability of a nation to shape the preferences of others through appeal and attraction rather than coercion. A country generates soft power through its culture (when it is pleasing to others), its political values (when it lives up to them at home and abroad), and its foreign policies (when they are seen as legitimate and having moral authority). For instance, the global ubiquity of Hollywood movies, American pop music, and democratic ideals did more to erode the ideological foundations of the Soviet Union during the Cold War than overt military threats. Thus, in an increasingly interconnected world, the ability to co-opt rather than coerce is becoming a paramount strategic asset.
question: It can be inferred from the passage that, according to the concept of 'soft power':
options: Military force is completely obsolete and should never be used in international relations.
Cultural appeal and ideological persuasion can be highly effective instruments of national strategy.
A country's foreign policy has no impact on how it is perceived by other nations.
Economic sanctions are considered a form of soft power because they do not involve physical violence.
answer: Cultural appeal and ideological persuasion can be highly effective instruments of national strategy.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि 'सॉफ्ट पावर' आकर्षण (appeal) और अनुनय (persuasion) के माध्यम से दूसरों की प्राथमिकताओं को आकार देने की क्षमता है (जैसे संस्कृति, मूल्य)। सोवियत संघ के खिलाफ हॉलीवुड और लोकतांत्रिक आदर्शों का उदाहरण यह साबित करता है कि सांस्कृतिक अपील और वैचारिक अनुनय सैन्य शक्ति जितने, या उससे अधिक प्रभावी रणनीतिक उपकरण (instruments of national strategy) हो सकते हैं।
trick: विकल्प A ('completely obsolete') अत्यधिक चरम (extreme) है। विकल्प D गलत है क्योंकि गद्यांश स्पष्ट रूप से 'economic sanctions' को 'hard power' कहता है। विकल्प B सही और तार्किक है।
tip: राजनीतिक विज्ञान (Political Science) के अनुच्छेदों में, Inference हमेशा उस नई रणनीति या सिद्धांत (Soft power) के लाभ को उजागर करता है जिसे लेखक ने प्रस्तुत किया है।

passage: Before the discovery of penicillin, Soviet and Eastern European scientists heavily researched 'phage therapy'—the use of bacteriophages (viruses that specifically infect and kill bacteria) to treat bacterial infections. However, with the mass production of broad-spectrum antibiotics in the West, phage therapy was largely dismissed as a cumbersome and obsolete relic of Soviet science. Today, this historical oversight is being frantically corrected. As the global crisis of antibiotic resistance renders our most powerful drugs increasingly ineffective, Western medicine is experiencing a renaissance of interest in bacteriophages. Unlike broad-spectrum antibiotics, which indiscriminately wipe out the body’s beneficial microbiome, phages are hyper-specific, targeting only a single strain of pathogenic bacteria while leaving the surrounding flora unharmed. Furthermore, because phages are living entities, they can evolve in real-time alongside muting bacteria, offering a dynamic countermeasure to the superbug crisis.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The reasons why Soviet medical science was historically superior to Western medicine.
The biological structure of bacteriophages and how they infect bacterial cells.
The resurgence of phage therapy as a vital, hyper-specific alternative to failing antibiotics.
The complete replacement of all modern antibiotics with viral therapies.
answer: The resurgence of phage therapy as a vital, hyper-specific alternative to failing antibiotics.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'फेज थेरेपी' (phage therapy) की वापसी (resurgence/renaissance) है। यह बताता है कि कैसे एंटीबायोटिक दवाओं के विफल होने (antibiotic resistance) के कारण पश्चिमी चिकित्सा फिर से इस पुराने, अति-विशिष्ट (hyper-specific) वायरल उपचार को अपना रही है। विकल्प C इस पूरे आख्यान को पूरी तरह से समेटता है।
trick: Main Theme गद्यांश की शुरुआत (Phage therapy), मध्य (crisis of antibiotics), और अंत (dynamic countermeasure) को जोड़ता है। केवल विकल्प C इन तीनों तत्वों को मिलाता है।
tip: चिकित्सा इतिहास के अनुच्छेदों में, यदि कोई पुरानी तकनीक (Old tech) वापस आ रही है, तो थीम हमेशा उस 'वापसी' (Resurgence/Renaissance) और उसके 'कारण' पर केंद्रित होती है।

passage: In his seminal book 'Bowling Alone,' sociologist Robert Putnam documented a severe and steady decline in 'social capital' in the United States since the mid-20th century. Social capital refers to the networks of relationships, trust, and reciprocity among people who live and work in a particular society. Putnam observed that participation in traditional civic organizations, neighborhood associations, and even recreational groups like bowling leagues had plummeted. He argued that this atomization of society, driven largely by suburban sprawl, increased screen time, and shifting work patterns, has profound civic consequences. When people stop interacting face-to-face in communal settings, their generalized trust in others and their engagement in the democratic process diminish. Consequently, a society devoid of robust social capital becomes highly fragmented, politically polarized, and structurally fragile.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred from Putnam's theory of 'social capital'?
options: The invention of the internet has significantly increased trust among local communities.
A decline in communal, face-to-face activities weakens civic engagement and societal stability.
Bowling leagues are the only effective way to build social trust in modern cities.
Suburban sprawl naturally encourages people to form tighter neighborhood associations.
answer: A decline in communal, face-to-face activities weakens civic engagement and societal stability.
explanation: गद्यांश में पटनम का तर्क है कि जब लोग सांप्रदायिक सेटिंग्स में आमने-सामने बातचीत (face-to-face in communal settings) करना बंद कर देते हैं, तो उनका विश्वास और लोकतांत्रिक जुड़ाव कम हो जाता है, जिससे समाज खंडित और नाजुक (structurally fragile) हो जाता है। इससे यह स्पष्ट अनुमान निकलता है कि सांप्रदायिक गतिविधियों में कमी नागरिक जुड़ाव और सामाजिक स्थिरता (societal stability) को कमज़ोर करती है।
trick: गद्यांश में 'When people stop interacting face-to-face... trust and engagement diminish' सीधे विकल्प B का समर्थन करता है।
tip: समाजशास्त्र (Sociology) के गद्यांशों में, जब 'Social Capital' या 'Community' की बात होती है, तो इसका सीधा संबंध हमेशा 'Civic engagement' और 'Democracy' की मजबूती से होता है।

passage: Following the completion of the Human Genome Project, scientists were initially baffled to discover that less than 2% of human DNA actually codes for proteins. The remaining 98% was hastily dismissed by many geneticists as 'junk DNA'—useless evolutionary baggage accumulated over millions of years. However, this dismissive nomenclature has proven to be a colossal scientific misstep. The ENCODE project later revealed that this so-called 'junk' is intensely biochemically active. Rather than being passive clutter, non-coding DNA functions as an intricate control panel, containing complex regulatory switches that dictate exactly when, where, and how robustly the protein-coding genes are turned on or off. Mutations within these non-coding regions are now known to be heavily implicated in a vast array of complex diseases, fundamentally rewriting our understanding of genomic architecture.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The failure of the Human Genome Project to sequence the entire human genetic code.
The biological process by which 'junk DNA' is physically removed from the human genome.
The paradigm shift showing that non-coding DNA plays a crucial regulatory role in genetics.
The superiority of non-coding DNA over protein-coding genes in evolutionary biology.
answer: The paradigm shift showing that non-coding DNA plays a crucial regulatory role in genetics.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय यह है कि जिसे पहले बेकार 'जंक डीएनए' (junk DNA) माना जाता था, वह वास्तव में व्यर्थ नहीं है, बल्कि जीन की अभिव्यक्ति को नियंत्रित करने वाला एक महत्वपूर्ण नियामक (regulatory control panel) है। यह नई खोज जीनोमिक वास्तुकला की हमारी समझ में एक बड़ा वैचारिक बदलाव (paradigm shift) है।
trick: गद्यांश 'misstep' (गलती) और 'rewriting our understanding' (हमारी समझ को फिर से लिखना) जैसे शब्दों का उपयोग करता है। यह स्पष्ट रूप से एक 'Paradigm shift' (प्रतिमान बदलाव) को दर्शाता है।
tip: विज्ञान के इतिहास में जब किसी चीज़ का नाम 'Junk' या 'Useless' रखा जाता है और बाद में वह उपयोगी साबित होती है, तो थीम हमेशा उस 'पुनर्मूल्यांकन' (Re-evaluation / Crucial role) पर केंद्रित होती है।

passage: In the aftermath of the Holocaust, psychologist Stanley Milgram sought to understand how ordinary citizens could participate in horrific atrocities. In his infamous 1961 experiment, volunteers were instructed by an authoritative figure in a lab coat to administer increasingly severe electric shocks to a 'learner' (an actor) whenever they answered a question incorrectly. Despite hearing the actor scream in feigned agony and plead for release, a staggering 65% of participants continued to administer shocks up to the maximum, supposedly lethal voltage, simply because the experimenter firmly stated, 'The experiment requires that you continue.' The Milgram experiment brutally shattered the comforting illusion that evil is perpetrated only by sociopaths. Instead, it demonstrated the terrifying power of situational variables, revealing that deep-seated obedience to perceived authority can easily override an individual's personal moral compass.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred from the results of the Milgram experiment?
options: Most human beings possess underlying sociopathic tendencies that enjoy causing pain.
Ordinary people can be coerced into committing harmful acts if directed by an established authority.
Electric shock therapy was an ineffective method for teaching learners new information.
Volunteers in the 1960s were significantly more obedient than people in modern society.
answer: Ordinary people can be coerced into committing harmful acts if directed by an established authority.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि मिलग्राम के प्रयोग ने इस भ्रम को तोड़ दिया कि केवल समाजोपथ (sociopaths) ही बुराई करते हैं। इसके बजाय, इसने दिखाया कि 'कथित अधिकार के प्रति गहरी आज्ञाकारिता व्यक्ति के व्यक्तिगत नैतिक कंपास को आसानी से खत्म कर सकती है' (obedience to perceived authority can easily override an individual's personal moral compass)। इसका स्पष्ट अनुमान है कि आम लोग (ordinary people) सत्ता/अधिकार के आदेश पर हानिकारक कृत्य कर सकते हैं।
trick: विकल्प A ('sociopathic tendencies') गद्यांश के ठीक विपरीत है, क्योंकि गद्यांश कहता है कि बुराई केवल समाजोपथ नहीं करते। विकल्प B प्रयोग का सही मनोवैज्ञानिक निष्कर्ष (Inference) है।
tip: मनोविज्ञान (Psychology) के क्लासिक प्रयोगों (जैसे Milgram, Zimbardo) पर आधारित गद्यांश हमेशा यह साबित करते हैं कि 'स्थिति' (Situation/Authority) व्यक्ति के 'स्वभाव' (Personality/Morals) से अधिक शक्तिशाली होती है।

passage: During the Cold War, the geopolitical standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union was governed by the terrifying strategic doctrine of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). The premise of MAD was rooted in deterrence theory: if both superpowers possessed arsenals of nuclear weapons robust enough to survive a first strike and retaliate with devastating force, neither side would dare initiate a conflict. In this macabre framework, the capability of total planetary annihilation paradoxically became the guarantor of global stability. However, this strategy required absolute rational calculation from both actors and infallible early-warning systems. Critics pointed out that MAD created a highly fragile peace, one perpetually vulnerable to accidental radar glitches, miscommunications, or the ascension of an irrational leader unbothered by the prospect of national suicide.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The engineering challenges involved in building early-warning radar systems during the Cold War.
The argument that nuclear weapons should be immediately dismantled to guarantee global peace.
The paradoxical doctrine where the threat of total nuclear annihilation functioned as a fragile deterrent to war.
The historical reasons why the Soviet Union ultimately lost the Cold War to the United States.
answer: The paradoxical doctrine where the threat of total nuclear annihilation functioned as a fragile deterrent to war.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'Mutually Assured Destruction' (MAD) सिद्धांत है, जो एक विरोधाभास (paradox) था: पूरी दुनिया को नष्ट करने की क्षमता ने ही शांति (guarantor of global stability) बनाए रखी। लेकिन साथ ही, यह शांति बहुत नाजुक (fragile) थी क्योंकि यह गलतफहमी या तकनीकी खराबी का शिकार हो सकती थी। विकल्प C इस पूरे विवरण को समेटता है।
trick: Main Theme हमेशा गद्यांश के मुख्य विरोधाभास (paradox) को पकड़ता है। 'Capability of total planetary annihilation paradoxically became the guarantor of global stability' सीधे विकल्प C से मेल खाता है।
tip: अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संबंधों (International Relations) और परमाणु रणनीतियों में, MAD (Mutually Assured Destruction) को हमेशा एक 'विरोधाभासी निवारक' (Paradoxical deterrent) के रूप में देखा जाता है।

passage: Technological determinism is the widespread belief that technology acts as an autonomous force, existing outside of society, that independently drives social and cultural change. From this viewpoint, the invention of the printing press caused the Reformation, and the smartphone caused modern social isolation. However, sociologists studying the Social Construction of Technology (SCOT) vehemently reject this reductionist narrative. They argue that technologies do not simply fall from the sky with inevitable consequences. Instead, human actors, economic interests, and cultural values continuously shape what technologies are funded, how they are designed, and the specific ways they are adopted or rejected. A smartphone is not inherently isolating; its isolating features are the result of deliberate design choices made by corporations aiming to maximize attention and profit. Thus, society shapes technology just as much as technology shapes society.
question: It can be reasonably inferred from the passage that advocates of the Social Construction of Technology (SCOT) believe:
options: The printing press had absolutely no impact on historical events like the Reformation.
Technologies are neutral tools whose impacts are entirely determined by human social contexts and choices.
Technological determinism accurately explains how the smartphone was invented.
Corporations should not be allowed to design technological devices like smartphones.
answer: Technologies are neutral tools whose impacts are entirely determined by human social contexts and choices.
explanation: SCOT (प्रौद्योगिकी का सामाजिक निर्माण) के पैरोकार मानते हैं कि तकनीक अपने आप में स्वायत्त या स्वतंत्र (autonomous force) नहीं है। यह मनुष्य, आर्थिक हितों और सांस्कृतिक मूल्यों (human actors, economic interests...) द्वारा आकार लेती है। इसका सीधा अनुमान यह है कि तकनीकें सामाजिक संदर्भों और मानवीय विकल्पों द्वारा निर्धारित (determined) होती हैं, न कि अपने आप परिणाम उत्पन्न करती हैं।
trick: 'society shapes technology just as much as technology shapes society' (समाज तकनीक को आकार देता है...) यह स्पष्ट करता है कि मानव विकल्प (human choices) तकनीक के प्रभाव को तय करते हैं।
tip: समाजशास्त्र (Sociology) में, जब 'Determinism' (नियतिवाद) को खारिज किया जाता है, तो हमेशा यह निष्कर्ष निकलता है कि 'मानव एजेंसी' (Human Agency) और 'सामाजिक संदर्भ' (Social Context) ही मुख्य प्रेरक शक्तियाँ हैं।

passage: At the ends of every human chromosome lie telomeres, repetitive sequences of non-coding DNA that act like the plastic tips on shoelaces, preventing the genetic strands from unraveling. Each time a cell divides, a small portion of the telomere is naturally consumed. Once telomeres reach a critically short length, the cell enters a state of permanent arrest known as senescence, effectively contributing to the physical deterioration we associate with aging. The discovery of telomerase—an enzyme capable of rebuilding telomeres—sparked immense excitement as a potential 'fountain of youth.' However, the biology of telomerase is fraught with peril. While increasing telomerase activity could theoretically rejuvenate aging tissues, it is exactly this mechanism that cancer cells hijack to achieve cellular immortality, allowing malignant tumors to grow unchecked. Modulating telomeres, therefore, represents a delicate tightrope walk between defying aging and provoking cancer.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The biological mechanism of cellular aging and the dangerous dual nature of manipulating telomerase.
The successful development of a cure for cancer using telomere-shortening enzymes.
The comparison between the structure of human chromosomes and the physical anatomy of shoelaces.
The failure of modern biology to understand how cells divide and repair themselves.
answer: The biological mechanism of cellular aging and the dangerous dual nature of manipulating telomerase.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय टीलोमर्स (telomeres) और एंजाइम 'टीलोमेरेज' (telomerase) की भूमिका को समझाना है। यह बताता है कि टीलोमेरेज उम्र बढ़ने को रोक सकता है (fountain of youth), लेकिन यही वह तंत्र है जिसका उपयोग कैंसर कोशिकाएं (cancer cells) अमर होने के लिए करती हैं। विकल्प A इस 'दोहरी प्रकृति' (dual nature) को सटीक रूप से सारांशित करता है।
trick: Main Theme = विवरण (Biological mechanism) + समस्या/चेतावनी (dangerous dual nature / tightrope walk). गद्यांश के अंत में दी गई चेतावनी ('tightrope walk') हमेशा थीम का हिस्सा होती है।
tip: बायोलॉजी के अनुच्छेदों में जब किसी खोज के फायदे और गंभीर नुकसान दोनों बताए जाएं, तो थीम में हमेशा 'Dual role', 'Double-edged sword', या 'Delicate balance' जैसे शब्द होते हैं।

passage: The 'Resource Curse,' or the paradox of plenty, refers to the counterintuitive phenomenon where countries with an abundance of non-renewable natural resources—such as oil, minerals, or precious metals—tend to experience less economic growth, less democracy, and worse developmental outcomes than countries with fewer natural resources. Economists attribute this to several intersecting factors. The sudden influx of resource wealth often causes the national currency to appreciate, rendering the country's other export sectors (like manufacturing or agriculture) globally uncompetitive, a process known as 'Dutch Disease.' Furthermore, this immense, centralized wealth creates extraordinary opportunities for political corruption and rent-seeking. Because autocratic regimes can sustain themselves entirely on resource revenues, they do not need to heavily tax their citizens, thereby severing the crucial link of accountability between the state and the public.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred from the passage regarding autocratic regimes in resource-rich nations?
options: They actively promote the manufacturing and agricultural sectors to diversify their economies.
They become highly responsive to public demands because they collect massive amounts of citizen taxes.
Their political survival relies more on controlling natural resources than on maintaining public consent.
They frequently suffer from severe budget deficits due to the depreciation of their national currency.
answer: Their political survival relies more on controlling natural resources than on maintaining public consent.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि निरंकुश शासन (autocratic regimes) पूरी तरह से संसाधन राजस्व (resource revenues) पर टिके रह सकते हैं। उन्हें नागरिकों पर कर (tax) लगाने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती, जिससे राज्य और जनता के बीच 'जवाबदेही की महत्वपूर्ण कड़ी' (link of accountability) टूट जाती है। इसका सीधा अनुमान यह है कि उनका राजनीतिक अस्तित्व जनता की सहमति (public consent / taxes) से अधिक प्राकृतिक संसाधनों को नियंत्रित करने पर निर्भर करता है।
trick: 'severing the crucial link of accountability between the state and the public' का सीधा अर्थ है कि उन्हें अब जनता की सहमति या परवाह (public consent) की आवश्यकता नहीं है।
tip: राजनीतिक अर्थशास्त्र (Political Economy) में 'Resource Curse' का मूल सिद्धांत ही यही है कि 'No taxation without representation' का उल्टा: 'No taxation means no representation' (जनता से कर नहीं लोगे, तो उनकी बात भी नहीं सुनोगे)।

passage: In 1967, French literary theorist Roland Barthes published a groundbreaking essay titled 'The Death of the Author.' Barthes argued against the traditional method of literary criticism, which sought to uncover the definitive meaning of a text by examining the biography, intentions, and historical context of its creator. According to Barthes, assigning a single, authorial intent imposes an artificial limit on a text. Instead, he posited that a piece of writing is a multidimensional space where a variety of writings blend and clash. Once a text is published, the 'author' conceptually dies, and the authority of interpretation passes entirely to the reader. Each reader brings their own subjective experiences and cultural codes to the text, generating a multiplicity of valid meanings. Thus, literature is not a monologue delivered by an authoritative creator, but an interactive collaboration born in the mind of the consumer.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The historical biographies of 20th-century French literary theorists.
The argument that authors must clearly state their intentions to avoid confusing the reader.
The philosophical shift in literary criticism from authorial intent to the reader's active interpretation.
The decline in the quality of literature following the widespread publication of 'The Death of the Author'.
answer: The philosophical shift in literary criticism from authorial intent to the reader's active interpretation.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय रोलां बार्थ के निबंध 'द डेथ ऑफ द ऑथर' पर चर्चा करना है, जिसने साहित्यिक आलोचना को लेखक के इरादे (authorial intent) से हटाकर पाठक की व्याख्या (reader's interpretation) पर केंद्रित कर दिया। लेखक अब पाठ का एकमात्र अर्थ तय नहीं करता, बल्कि पाठक अपने अनुभव से नए अर्थ निकालता है।
trick: Main Theme गद्यांश के मुख्य बदलाव को दर्शाता है: 'away from traditional method (author)' -> 'authority passes entirely to the reader'. विकल्प C इस 'shift' (बदलाव) को सटीक रूप से पकड़ता है।
tip: साहित्यिक सिद्धांत (Literary Theory) के अनुच्छेदों में, 'Death of the Author' या 'Post-structuralism' हमेशा इस बात पर ज़ोर देते हैं कि 'अर्थ' (Meaning) निश्चित नहीं है, बल्कि 'पाठक' (Reader) द्वारा बनाया जाता है।

passage: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), developed by John Sweller, revolutionized instructional design by anchoring teaching methods directly to the biological architecture of human memory. Human cognition consists of a vast, nearly limitless long-term memory and a highly restricted working memory, which can typically hold only a handful of novel 'chunks' of information at a time. CLT categorizes mental effort into three types: intrinsic (the inherent difficulty of the subject), extraneous (effort caused by poor instructional formatting), and germane (effort dedicated to schema construction). When educators present new material using overly cluttered slides, redundant text, or distracting background music, they drastically increase the extraneous load. If the total cognitive load exceeds the working memory's capacity, a bottleneck occurs, preventing the transfer of information into long-term memory, thereby halting the learning process entirely.
question: Which of the following can be reasonably inferred from Cognitive Load Theory?
options: Working memory has a significantly larger storage capacity than long-term memory.
Instructional designs that overwhelm working memory are fundamentally ineffective for long-term learning.
Educators should strive to increase extraneous load to make learning more challenging and engaging.
Human cognition relies entirely on long-term memory, rendering working memory biologically useless.
answer: Instructional designs that overwhelm working memory are fundamentally ineffective for long-term learning.
explanation: गद्यांश स्पष्ट रूप से बताता है कि मानव की 'वर्किंग मेमोरी' (working memory) अत्यधिक सीमित है। यदि कुल संज्ञानात्मक भार (cognitive load) इस क्षमता से अधिक हो जाता है (overwhelms), तो जानकारी 'लॉन्ग-टर्म मेमोरी' (long-term memory) में स्थानांतरित नहीं हो पाती है, जिससे सीखने की प्रक्रिया पूरी तरह रुक जाती है ('halting the learning process entirely')। इसलिए, भारी या अव्यवस्थित निर्देश अप्रभावी होते हैं।
trick: अंतिम वाक्य ('If the total cognitive load exceeds the working memory's capacity... halting the learning process entirely') का सीधा अर्थ (inference) विकल्प B है।
tip: शिक्षा शास्त्र (Pedagogy) या मनोविज्ञान के गद्यांशों में, यदि किसी मानवीय क्षमता (जैसे Memory) की कोई सीमा (limit) बताई गई है, तो Inference हमेशा उस सीमा के पार जाने पर होने वाले 'विनाशकारी परिणाम' (failure of learning) पर आधारित होता है।

passage: One of the more unsettling solutions proposed for the Fermi Paradox is the 'Zoo Hypothesis,' formulated by astronomer John A. Ball in 1973. This hypothesis assumes that advanced extraterrestrial civilizations are ubiquitous in the galaxy, yet they have collectively agreed to avoid any contact with Earth. Just as human beings set aside pristine wildlife sanctuaries to allow nature to develop without interference, a galactic community might view humanity as a primitive, developing species worthy of observation but deeply vulnerable to cultural contamination. According to this premise, the cosmic silence we observe is not a natural void, but an artificial quarantine imposed by vastly superior beings. The terrifying corollary of the Zoo Hypothesis is that our scientific understanding of the universe is fundamentally incomplete, as we are being deliberately deceived by an invisible, omnipotent audience.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The scientific proof that extraterrestrial civilizations frequently visit Earth disguised as animals.
A theoretical solution to the Fermi Paradox suggesting Earth is deliberately isolated and observed by advanced aliens.
The necessity of building better telescopes to break through the artificial quarantine around Earth.
The environmental argument for creating more wildlife sanctuaries on Earth to protect primitive species.
answer: A theoretical solution to the Fermi Paradox suggesting Earth is deliberately isolated and observed by advanced aliens.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'ज़ू हाइपोथिसिस' (Zoo Hypothesis) है, जो फर्मी पैराडॉक्स का एक सैद्धांतिक समाधान प्रस्तुत करता है। यह सिद्धांत बताता है कि उन्नत एलियंस मौजूद हैं, लेकिन वे जानबूझकर पृथ्वी से संपर्क से बच रहे हैं (deliberately isolated) और हमें एक वन्यजीव अभयारण्य (wildlife sanctuary) की तरह देख रहे हैं।
trick: Main Theme हमेशा गद्यांश की मुख्य अवधारणा (Zoo Hypothesis) और उसकी परिभाषा (isolated and observed by aliens) को जोड़ता है।
tip: खगोल विज्ञान (Astronomy) या एलियन परिकल्पनाओं वाले गद्यांशों में, उन विकल्पों से बचें जो 'scientific proof' (वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण) का दावा करते हैं (जैसे विकल्प A)। ये केवल 'Theoretical solutions' (सैद्धांतिक समाधान) होते हैं।

passage: In the philosophy of mind, addressing the 'hard problem of consciousness'—how subjective experience arises from non-conscious physical matter—has led some contemporary thinkers to resurrect a deeply ancient, somewhat counterintuitive theory: panpsychism. Traditional physicalism struggles to pinpoint the exact moment or mechanism by which a complex arrangement of neurons suddenly 'wakes up' and experiences the color red or the feeling of pain. Panpsychism circumvents this magic trick by positing that consciousness is not an emergent anomaly generated by complex brains, but rather a fundamental, ubiquitous property of the physical universe, much like mass or electrical charge. According to this view, even elementary particles possess incredibly rudimentary forms of subjective experience. While heavily criticized as untestable metaphysics, panpsychism offers a mathematically elegant continuity, asserting that human consciousness is merely a highly complex aggregation of the consciousness inherent in all matter.
question: It can be inferred from the passage that a proponent of 'panpsychism' would believe that:
options: Consciousness is an illusion created entirely by religious institutions.
Only highly evolved biological brains possess the capacity for subjective experience.
Consciousness does not magically appear at a certain level of biological complexity; it is a fundamental property of all matter.
The 'hard problem of consciousness' can be easily solved by studying the electrical charge of the human heart.
answer: Consciousness does not magically appear at a certain level of biological complexity; it is a fundamental property of all matter.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि पैनसाइकिज्म (panpsychism) यह मानता है कि चेतना अचानक किसी जटिल मस्तिष्क से उत्पन्न (emergent anomaly) नहीं होती, बल्कि यह ब्रह्मांड का एक मौलिक गुण (fundamental property) है, ठीक द्रव्यमान (mass) की तरह। यहाँ तक कि प्राथमिक कणों (elementary particles) में भी इसका मूल रूप होता है। इसका सीधा अनुमान यह है कि चेतना सभी पदार्थों का एक मूलभूत गुण है।
trick: गद्यांश में 'circumvents this magic trick by positing that consciousness is not an emergent anomaly... but rather a fundamental... property of the physical universe' सीधे विकल्प C का समर्थन करता है।
tip: दर्शनशास्त्र (Philosophy of Mind) में 'Panpsychism' का अर्थ ही है 'Pan' (सभी जगह) + 'Psych' (चेतना)। यानी चेतना हर पदार्थ में मौजूद है।

passage: In the realm of mathematics and meteorology, 'Chaos Theory' fundamentally subverted the Newtonian dream of a perfectly predictable, clockwork universe. The theory was popularized by Edward Lorenz in the 1960s, who discovered that weather simulation models were extraordinarily sensitive to their initial conditions. Entering a data point as 0.506 instead of 0.506127—a minuscule rounding difference of less than one part in a thousand—produced a completely divergent weather forecast weeks later. This phenomenon, famously dubbed the 'Butterfly Effect,' posits that the flap of a butterfly's wings in Brazil could theoretically set off a cascade of atmospheric events culminating in a tornado in Texas. Chaos theory demonstrates that even in entirely deterministic systems governed by strict physical laws, long-term prediction is fundamentally impossible because we can never measure the initial conditions of the universe with infinite precision.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The biological impact of butterflies on global weather patterns and atmospheric pressure.
The historical failure of Edward Lorenz to accurately predict the weather in the 1960s.
How minute initial variations in complex deterministic systems lead to vastly divergent and unpredictable outcomes.
The proof that the universe operates without any strict physical laws or deterministic mathematical rules.
answer: How minute initial variations in complex deterministic systems lead to vastly divergent and unpredictable outcomes.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'कैओस थ्योरी' (Chaos Theory) और 'बटरफ्लाई इफेक्ट' है। यह समझाता है कि कैसे जटिल, नियतात्मक प्रणालियों (deterministic systems) में बहुत छोटे प्रारंभिक अंतर (minute initial variations) एक विशाल और अप्रत्याशित परिणाम (unpredictable outcomes) की ओर ले जाते हैं, जिससे दीर्घकालिक भविष्यवाणी असंभव हो जाती है।
trick: विकल्प D गलत है क्योंकि गद्यांश स्पष्ट रूप से कहता है 'deterministic systems governed by strict physical laws' (कठोर भौतिक नियमों द्वारा शासित)। विकल्प C गद्यांश की सटीक थीम है।
tip: विज्ञान के अनुच्छेदों में रूपकों (Metaphors - जैसे Butterfly flapping wings) को शाब्दिक (literal) अर्थ में नहीं लेना चाहिए (विकल्प A गलत है)। वे हमेशा एक गहरे गणितीय या भौतिक सिद्धांत (Minute variations = huge effects) को दर्शाते हैं।

passage: The ideology of 'meritocracy'—the notion that individuals succeed solely based on their talent and hard work—is often heralded as the ultimate egalitarian ideal. In a true meritocracy, social class, race, and inherited wealth supposedly surrender to individual exertion. However, critical sociologists argue that in highly unequal societies, the rhetoric of meritocracy functions as a deceptive legitimizing myth. Because access to high-quality education, healthcare, and influential social networks is overwhelmingly determined by the socioeconomic status of one’s parents, the 'starting line' of the societal race is staggeringly uneven. When those who begin with immense inherited advantages cross the finish line first, the ideology of meritocracy allows them to claim their success was entirely self-made. Consequently, this narrative is doubly cruel: it flatters the privileged while implicitly blaming the marginalized for their own structural disenfranchisement.
question: It can be inferred from the passage that the rhetoric of meritocracy in unequal societies serves to:
options: Level the playing field by providing equal access to education and healthcare for everyone.
Obscure systemic structural inequalities by falsely attributing success solely to individual effort.
Encourage the marginalized to overthrow the privileged through violent revolution.
Prove definitively that inherited wealth has no impact on a person's future career.
answer: Obscure systemic structural inequalities by falsely attributing success solely to individual effort.
explanation: गद्यांश में कहा गया है कि असमान समाजों में योग्यता (meritocracy) का विचार एक 'धोखा देने वाला वैध मिथक' (deceptive legitimizing myth) है। यह उन लोगों को अपनी सफलता का श्रेय 'पूरी तरह से खुद' (entirely self-made) को देने की अनुमति देता है, जिन्होंने वास्तव में विरासत में मिले फायदों (inherited advantages) का उपयोग किया है। इससे अनुमान निकलता है कि योग्यता का यह दावा प्रणालीगत असमानताओं (systemic inequalities) को छिपाने (obscure) का काम करता है।
trick: वाक्य 'allows them to claim their success was entirely self-made' और 'blaming the marginalized for their own structural disenfranchisement' सीधे विकल्प B का समर्थन करते हैं।
tip: सामाजिक विज्ञान (Social Sciences) के अनुच्छेदों में जब 'Myth' या 'Ideology' शब्द का प्रयोग आलोचनात्मक ढंग से होता है, तो Inference हमेशा यही होता है कि यह विचारधारा 'सच्चाई (असमानता) को छिपाने' (hiding the truth / inequality) का काम करती है।

passage: In the latter half of the 20th century, political scientist James Flynn uncovered a staggering statistical anomaly: global IQ scores were consistently rising by roughly three points every decade. This phenomenon, termed the 'Flynn Effect,' posed a massive challenge to the prevailing belief that intelligence is a strictly innate, genetically fixed trait. Human genetics cannot evolve rapidly enough to account for a massive multi-generational leap in cognitive test scores. Therefore, psychologists concluded that the increase must be driven by profound environmental shifts. Improvements in childhood nutrition, the near-universal expansion of formal education, the reduction of infectious diseases, and an increasingly complex, visually stimulating technological environment have all heavily subsidized modern brain development. The Flynn Effect compellingly suggests that human intellectual potential is highly elastic, deeply responsive to the societal ecosystem in which an individual is nurtured.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The genetic mutations responsible for the rapid evolution of human intelligence in the 20th century.
The failure of traditional IQ tests to accurately measure biological intelligence.
The persistent rise in global IQ scores and its attribution to beneficial environmental and societal shifts.
The negative impact of technology and visually stimulating environments on childhood development.
answer: The persistent rise in global IQ scores and its attribution to beneficial environmental and societal shifts.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'फ्लिन प्रभाव' (Flynn Effect) है, जो वैश्विक IQ स्कोर में निरंतर वृद्धि को दर्शाता है। गद्यांश यह स्पष्ट करता है कि यह वृद्धि आनुवंशिकी (genetics) के कारण नहीं है, बल्कि सकारात्मक पर्यावरणीय बदलावों (nutrition, education, technology) के कारण है। विकल्प C इस पूरी अवधारणा को सही ढंग से प्रस्तुत करता है।
trick: Main Theme = घटना (Rise in IQ scores) + उसका कारण (Environmental/societal shifts). विकल्प A गलत है क्योंकि गद्यांश आनुवंशिकी (genetics) को खारिज करता है।
tip: वैज्ञानिक खोजों (जैसे Flynn Effect) पर आधारित गद्यांशों में थीम हमेशा खोज (Discovery) और उसके निष्कर्ष (Conclusion/Cause) का एक संयोजन होती है।

passage: The concept of the 'hedonic treadmill,' developed by psychologists Brickman and Campbell in the 1970s, posits a profoundly sobering view of human happiness. The theory suggests that humans possess a relatively stable, genetically determined baseline level of happiness. When individuals experience major life events—whether overwhelmingly positive, like winning the lottery, or tragically negative, like suffering a paralyzing injury—they predictably display a sharp spike or drop in subjective well-being. However, this shift is almost entirely transitory. Due to a psychological process called 'hedonic adaptation,' the initial intense emotions inevitably fade, and individuals gradually habituate to their new circumstances, eventually returning to their original emotional baseline. This phenomenon explains why the relentless pursuit of material wealth often feels empty; securing a higher standard of living merely resets expectations, leaving the individual running furiously just to stay in the same emotional place.
question: Which of the following can be most reasonably inferred from the concept of the 'hedonic treadmill'?
options: People who win the lottery will remain significantly happier than the general population for the rest of their lives.
Major life events only temporarily alter a person's emotional state before they adapt to the new reality.
Human happiness is completely unpredictable and has no connection to a person's genetic makeup.
Experiencing a tragic injury permanently destroys a person's ability to ever feel happiness again.
answer: Major life events only temporarily alter a person's emotional state before they adapt to the new reality.
explanation: गद्यांश स्पष्ट रूप से बताता है कि चाहे कुछ बहुत अच्छा हो (लॉटरी) या बहुत बुरा (चोट), भावनाओं में बदलाव 'लगभग पूरी तरह से अस्थायी' (almost entirely transitory) होता है। 'हेडोनिक अनुकूलन' (hedonic adaptation) के कारण व्यक्ति अपने नए हालात का आदी हो जाता है और अपनी पुरानी भावनात्मक स्थिति (baseline) पर लौट आता है। इसलिए, बड़ी जीवन घटनाएं केवल अस्थायी रूप से (temporarily) भावनात्मक स्थिति को बदलती हैं।
trick: 'this shift is almost entirely transitory' और 'gradually habituate to their new circumstances' सीधे तौर पर विकल्प B का समर्थन करते हैं। विकल्प A और D गद्यांश के बिल्कुल विपरीत हैं।
tip: मनोविज्ञान (Psychology) में 'Adaptation' या 'Habituation' का मतलब हमेशा यही होता है कि इंसान किसी भी नई चीज़ (अच्छी या बुरी) का आदी हो जाता है और उसका असर खत्म हो जाता है (temporary effect)।

passage: In 1965, Gordon Moore posited a simple but revolutionary observation that would guide the tech industry for over half a century: the number of transistors on a microchip doubles roughly every two years, exponentially decreasing the cost of computing power while massively increasing its capability. This axiom, known as Moore’s Law, is the foundational rhythm behind the digital revolution, driving everything from the internet to artificial intelligence. However, engineers are now facing the inescapable boundaries of physical reality. As transistors shrink to the size of a few atoms, they encounter severe problems with heat dissipation and 'quantum tunneling'—a phenomenon where electrons unpredictably leak across barriers, corrupting data. While the industry is furiously pivoting toward novel architectures like 3D stacking and quantum computing, the era of predictable, exponential silicon scaling that defined Moore’s Law is definitively grinding to a halt.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The superiority of quantum computing over traditional silicon-based microchips.
The historical impact of Gordon Moore on the development of the artificial intelligence industry.
The physical and scientific barriers that are bringing an end to the exponential growth predicted by Moore's Law.
The reasons why tech companies are intentionally slowing down the production of microchips to raise prices.
answer: The physical and scientific barriers that are bringing an end to the exponential growth predicted by Moore's Law.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय मूर के नियम (Moore's Law) का परिचय देना और फिर यह बताना है कि कैसे भौतिक वास्तविकता की सीमाएं (Physical reality, heat dissipation, quantum tunneling) अब इस नियम के अनुसार होने वाले घातीय विकास (exponential growth) को समाप्त कर रही हैं ('grinding to a halt')। विकल्प C इस पूरे विवरण का सटीक सारांश है।
trick: Main Theme हमेशा गद्यांश के मुख्य संघर्ष (conflict) को पकड़ता है। यहाँ संघर्ष 'Moore's Law (विकास)' और 'Physical boundaries (रुकावट)' के बीच है।
tip: प्रौद्योगिकी (Technology) के गद्यांशों में 'However' के बाद आने वाला हिस्सा हमेशा सबसे महत्वपूर्ण होता है। यहाँ 'However' के बाद की भौतिक सीमाएं (Physical boundaries) ही गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय हैं।

passage: Rational Choice Theory (RCT) has heavily dominated classical economics and political science, proposing a straightforward model of human behavior: individuals are fundamentally selfish, calculating actors. According to RCT, before making any decision—from voting in an election to committing a crime or choosing a spouse—a person conducts a rapid, internal cost-benefit analysis. They will always select the action that maximizes their personal utility and minimizes their costs. However, while RCT provides a mathematically elegant framework for modeling aggregate market behaviors, sociologists frequently critique its brutal reductionism. Critics argue that RCT completely fails to account for altruism, deeply ingrained cultural norms, spontaneous emotional reactions, and social obligations that frequently compel individuals to act in ways that are highly detrimental to their own immediate self-interest.
question: It can be reasonably inferred from the passage that critics of Rational Choice Theory believe:
options: Human social behavior is far too complex and emotionally driven to be reduced to mere cost-benefit calculations.
Individuals never conduct cost-benefit analyses when making important financial decisions.
Rational Choice Theory is the only framework that accurately explains altruism and cultural norms.
Sociologists should completely abandon the study of human emotions and focus only on market behaviors.
answer: Human social behavior is far too complex and emotionally driven to be reduced to mere cost-benefit calculations.
explanation: गद्यांश बताता है कि समाजशास्त्री (sociologists) रैशनल चॉइस थ्योरी (RCT) की निंदा करते हैं क्योंकि यह 'परमार्थ' (altruism), 'सांस्कृतिक मानदंडों' (cultural norms) और 'भावनात्मक प्रतिक्रियाओं' (emotional reactions) को ध्यान में नहीं रखता। इसका सीधा अनुमान यह है कि आलोचकों का मानना है कि मानव व्यवहार बहुत जटिल और भावनात्मक है, जिसे केवल 'लागत-लाभ विश्लेषण' (cost-benefit calculations) तक सीमित (reduced) नहीं किया जा सकता।
trick: गद्यांश में 'critique its brutal reductionism' (इसकी क्रूर न्यूनीकरणवाद की आलोचना) का अर्थ है कि RCT मानव व्यवहार को बहुत सरल बना देता है, जबकि असल में वह बहुत जटिल (complex) है।
tip: जब भी किसी थ्योरी को 'Reductionist' (न्यूनीकरणवादी) कहा जाता है, तो इसका मतलब होता है कि वह थ्योरी एक बहुत जटिल विषय (complex issue) को बहुत सरल तरीके से समझाने की कोशिश कर रही है, जो कि उसकी सबसे बड़ी कमी (flaw) है।

passage: The burgeoning, interdisciplinary field of 'neuroaesthetics' attempts to bridge the seemingly unbridgeable chasm between objective neuroscience and the subjective appreciation of art. Pioneers in this field utilize brain-imaging technologies like fMRI to map the neural correlates of aesthetic pleasure, discovering that observing a beautiful painting or listening to a symphony triggers robust activity in the brain's reward centers, identical to the neurological pathways activated by food or evolutionary survival mechanisms. This suggests that the human appreciation of beauty is not merely a superfluous cultural byproduct, but a deeply ingrained biological drive. However, humanist critics caution against biological reductionism. They argue that while science can map the dopamine spikes associated with viewing a Van Gogh, it can never quantify the profound, localized cultural context and historical grief that truly give the artwork its transcendent meaning.
question: What is the primary theme of the passage?
options: The scientific proof that listening to a symphony is biologically more important than eating food.
The attempt by neuroaesthetics to biological explain the appreciation of beauty, and the philosophical criticism of this approach.
The complete rejection of neuroscience by artists and humanists in the modern era.
The ways in which fMRI technology has been used to create new, historically transcendent artwork.
answer: The attempt by neuroaesthetics to biological explain the appreciation of beauty, and the philosophical criticism of this approach.
explanation: गद्यांश का मुख्य विषय 'न्यूरोएस्थेटिक्स' (neuroaesthetics) के क्षेत्र का परिचय देना है (जो कला की सुंदरता को जैविक और न्यूरोलॉजिकल रूप से समझाने की कोशिश करता है) और फिर इसका विरोध करने वाले मानवतावादी आलोचकों (humanist critics) की चेतावनी प्रस्तुत करना है जो मानते हैं कि विज्ञान कला के सांस्कृतिक और ऐतिहासिक अर्थ को नहीं माप सकता। विकल्प B इस दोहरे दृष्टिकोण (dual perspective) को पूरी तरह से पकड़ता है।
trick: Main Theme हमेशा गद्यांश की संरचना का पालन करता है: 1) New Science (Neuroaesthetics explores beauty biologically) + 2) Criticism (Humanists warn against reductionism).
tip: विज्ञान (Science) बनाम कला/मानविकी (Art/Humanities) वाले गद्यांशों में, थीम हमेशा दोनों के बीच के 'तनाव' (Tension) या 'पूरकता' (Complementarity) को दर्शाती है। कोई भी एक पक्ष पूरी तरह से जीतता या हारता नहीं है।
